item.title: Building a computer that can pause and resume in milliseconds: Inside the MicroVM architecture behind Managed Agents (20 minute read)
item.description: DigitalOcean's Firecracker platform separates agent sessions from their hosts using checkpointed disk, memory, and virtual-device state, with lazy loading to avoid downloading whole snapshots before resuming. Internal tests report under 200 milliseconds at p50 on the warm-template path, while external connections and API side effects remain outside the checkpoint.

item.title: Build the agent. Don't build its computer (20 minute read)
item.description: Agent teams should specify their execution environment, test recovery on real workloads, and start with managed infrastructure unless ownership offers a concrete advantage. The evaluation checklist covers persistent files, expired logins, interrupted external actions, access boundaries, and cost per accepted result.

item.title: How Meta Built Forum With AI-Native Engineering (8 minute read)
item.description: Meta built Forum with agents participating in planning, implementation, testing, and verification while engineers retained architectural judgment and final sign-off. The team improved results through simpler code, tools that inspect live app state, repeatable UI stress tests, and a separate build that excludes prototype code from production.

item.title: What I Self-Host (15 minute read)
item.description: A home server runs 28 services, including Jellyfin, Immich, Home Assistant, and Vaultwarden, on a mini PC with 16 GB of RAM. The setup favors simple native services and systemd-managed Podman containers, keeps services behind a VPN, and rejects tools whose operational complexity outweighs their value.

item.title: Code Is a Commodity Now (11 minute read)
item.description: Cheaper code generation could push software agencies away from selling development hours and toward domain expertise, product judgment, and accountability for outcomes. The essay argues that smaller generalist teams and changing hiring signals follow from this shift, while acknowledging mixed productivity evidence and the cost of verifying changes in mature codebases.

item.title: How to Measure the Human Cost of Agent Work (8 minute read)
item.description: Measure agent workflows by the human effort and agent spend required to reach an accepted result, including time spent briefing, supervising, reviewing, correcting, and verifying the work. Keep failed attempts and manual rescues in the totals so successful tasks do not hide the cost of unsuccessful ones. Track quality and later defects alongside time, and compare similar tasks under the same acceptance criteria before claiming productivity gains.

item.title: Vector search can't tell which memory is current (Sponsor)
item.description: Plain vector retrieval returns the old preference and the new one, and passing stale context to an LLM leads to hallucinations and conflicting actions. Graph-aware retrieval fixes this at the database layer with typed edges linking each memory to the one it replaced, and lifecycle flags marking what's active. The agent gets a clean current state, and the full history stays intact. Read the technical breakdown & companion notebook

item.title: Deploy with Void (7 minute read)
item.description: Void combines an open-source deployment platform, SDK, and CLI to bring full-stack development and Cloudflare deployment into a Vite workflow. It infers resource bindings and provisions infrastructure during deployment, while the shared platform lets administrators control team access, resource limits, and deployments.

item.title: Muse Spark Open (4 minute read)
item.description: Meta has released Muse Spark Open, a multimodal model with 816 billion total parameters, 42 billion active parameters, and a one-million-token context window. It supports coding and agentic workflows through hosted APIs or local inference, including on two M5 Ultra Mac Studios, with weights available under a license that includes limited commercial terms.

item.title: Introducing Devin Oncall (11 minute read)
item.description: Devin Oncall is generally available for investigating and remediating production issues, using company-specific skills and memory alongside a coding agent. Responders group related alerts and skip known issues, while an asynchronous review agent challenges unsupported diagnoses and premature conclusions.

item.title: What today's software owes to Bronze Age clocks (9 minute read)
item.description: Leaky buckets provide cheap admission control by calculating available capacity from a stored level and timestamp whenever new work arrives. The article connects this approach to API rate limits and PlanetScale's Postgres Traffic Control, which uses resource budgets to admit or block queries before execution and recommends testing budgets in warning mode first.

item.title: How Close Are We To Fully Autonomous Chip Design? (21 minute read)
item.description: Synopsys describes using orchestrated task agents to turn specifications into verified RTL, while full autonomy through physical implementation and chip sign-off remains a goal. Human engineers still define architectures and approve manufacturing, with advanced packaging and physical AI adding demands for coordinated multiphysics analysis.

The account traces the shift toward local workflows, a shared Rust agent core, and models trained for interactive work in messy codebases.

item.title: Open weight takes 71.5% of tokens and 23% of spend (7 minute read)

item.title: How we made a 9 MB WebAssembly module feel faster without removing a single byte (11 minute read)
item.description: Earlier loading, preload hints, and shared initialization promises made a 9.2 MB Skia WebAssembly module render its first canvas roughly 17% to 18% faster in the reported A/B test without meaningfully shrinking the download.

item.description: Long agentic reinforcement-learning rollouts make harness state, tool-call serialization, branching trajectories, and numerical differences between inference and training harder to keep consistent.

item.title: The Most Common Questions About Agent Evals, Answered (8 minute read)
item.description: Agent evals score runs against desired behaviors, but exact-output tests often fail because agent outputs and paths vary. item.title: Lazy Loading Images and Media: How Far Ahead Browsers Fetch (6 minute read)
item.description: Browsers fetch lazy-loaded media at different distances, with Chrome adjusting its margin based on connection speed, Firefox using a fixed 600-pixel threshold, and Safari applying a viewport-based threshold to images. The article explains why the largest contentful paint image should load eagerly and why media dimensions should be reserved to prevent layout shifts. Its practical takeaway is to use native lazy loading selectively, based on how far ahead each browser fetches.

item.title: From 2,500 requests to 24: Rebuilding star history without the stargazers (7 minute read)
item.description: GitHub rebuilt its star-history API to return up to 30 weeks of daily counts in one request. Maintainers can track a project's momentum without exposing stargazer identities, which could be scraped for spam or phishing. To avoid simply shifting the cost to count queries, the endpoint filters stars by time before counting, reducing database work.

item.title: Pure UI in the Agentic Era (6 minute read)
item.description: The article revisits the idea that UI should be a pure function of state and explains why it matters for agent-written interfaces. Passing roles, plans, billing status, and feature flags explicitly lets teams render and inspect each state combination before release.

item.title: Passkeys Are Not a Trap (4 minute read)
item.description: Synced consumer passkeys generally return no attestation, and WebAuthn attestation identifies an authenticator model rather than a user's operating system, browser, or firmware. The response argues that passkeys remain more phishing-resistant than TOTP and recommends continuing to use them.

item.title: A Year of Fast Apply: The Path to 10k Tokens per Second (13 minute read)
item.description: Relace explains how it built a small model that applies code edits at a reported 10,000 tokens per second using high-quality merge data, LoRA fine-tuning, FP8 quantization, and speculative decoding. Relace Apply 3 supports a 256,000-token context and multiple diff formats, although improving frontier-model edit accuracy could eventually reduce the need for specialized apply models.

item.title: How I Found a $90,000 Remote Code Execution Vulnerability in Google (4 minute read)
item.description: Google's DevSite stored an OAuth secret inside a readable Flask session cookie and reused it as the cookie's signing key, allowing forged sessions to reach unsafe pickle deserialization. Timing-based tests confirmed unauthenticated code execution across the shared platform, earning a $90,000 bounty. The fix separates signing keys from OAuth credentials and removes sensitive serialized objects from client-controlled sessions.

item.title: Can we Make React Faster using the React Compiler? (20 minute read)
item.description: React Compiler uses cache slots and tracks values that change together to avoid unnecessary work. In a 2,000-row microbenchmark, inlining alone slowed rendering from 444 ms to 1,038 ms by removing per-row caches, while adding block DOM updates cut it to 164 ms. These prototypes illustrate optimization opportunities, with workload and memory tradeoffs still to evaluate.

item.title: Building Shared Workspaces for People and Agents (10 minute read)
item.description: Perplexity Projects uses a lightweight Git forge backed by S3 storage so people and agents can build on durable files from isolated, temporary sandboxes. In production, fewer than 2% of submissions are rejected as stale, with median submit latency below 1.7 seconds.

item.title: Human PR Review Is Next (12 minute read)
item.description: AI code review will increasingly replace reading every diff, shifting human work toward requirements, acceptance testing, and ownership of releases. A trading-bot rounding bug illustrates the tradeoff: fast fixes do not erase losses or compensate for gaps in the specification.

item.title: Why WebMCP Matters (9 minute read)
item.description: WebMCP lets websites expose JavaScript tools to agents, reducing the slow, brittle interaction of navigating through screenshots and DOM inspection while keeping users in a shared browser session. Shopify's checkout experiment reported 2.7 times faster execution, 58% lower cost, and 60 successful attempts out of 60 compared with 56 for browser automation. Permissions, human approval signals, and testing against complete agent systems remain open challenges.

The advice favors shared infrastructure, observable tool calls, small targeted evals, and UI for reviewing and undoing agent actions.

item.description: The GoDaddy Developer Platform connects hosting, domains, and professional email in one programmable workflow, accessible from your code, scripts, or AI agents.Deploy Node.js apps through APIs or the gddy CLI. Then use the APIs to register a domain, configure DNS, and set up professional email.One platform identity, consistent API conventions, and shared documentation connect each step. Access developer pricing on eligible domain registrations.→ Explore the APIs→ See domain pricing

item.title: We built our own cloud agents runtime. Here's what we learned (11 minute read)
item.description: PostHog describes the shared runtime behind its Desktop, Slack, self-driving, and web agents, built around Temporal workflows, VM sandboxes, snapshots, fresh credentials, and resumable run logs. The hard-won lessons cover queued follow-ups, deterministic network controls, Docker-capable custom images, and designing every run to survive the loss of its sandbox.

item.title: How ChatGPT Intelligent UI works (20 minute read)
item.description: A reverse-engineering tour traces ChatGPT's interactive responses from a model-written DIL format through server-side compilation, sandboxed client execution, and native rendering. It also explains how streaming recompiles partial output, preserves keyed state, and sends server-resolved data such as images separately from model text.

item.title: Chrome Decisions API: the prompts, limits, engines and code reviews behind DecisionModel (10 minute read)
item.description: An investigation of Chrome's experimental Decisions API compares the explainer with implementation code and review comments. It surfaces slow Gemma 4 timings, position bias, context limits, probability semantics, and differences between Chrome's prototype and MediaPipe's DecisionMaker.

item.title: When code is cheap, judgement becomes the job (11 minute read)
item.description: As AI makes code production cheap, the scarce work shifts to choosing priorities, reviewing product behavior, maintaining architecture, and owning outcomes in production. Senior engineers create leverage by turning repeated review feedback into guidance and deterministic lint rules while keeping human judgment for business context.

item.title: Don't merge what you didn't run: a test gate for agent-written code (10 minute read)
item.description: A practical test gate checks agent-written changes on a clean machine before review by reinstalling from scratch, running the full suite three times, rejecting removed or skipped tests, and restoring the base branch's tests against the new code. Running the same gate inside the agent loop turns failures into immediate repair instructions while an independent CI run keeps the verdict outside the agent's control.

item.title: Treg (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Treg acts as an OpenRouter for agent tools, giving agents one base URL and token for a catalog of metered provider endpoints plus team-owned APIs, CLIs, and skills. It can inject credentials server-side, expose tools through MCP and agent skills, and let teams share capabilities without placing provider keys in callers.

item.title: Plannotator (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Plannotator provides a local browser-based review surface for plans, Markdown, HTML artifacts, diffs, and pull requests produced by coding agents. Hooks and commands route annotations back to agents, with support for multiple agent harnesses and local-first storage by default.

item.title: A Single POST Freezes Any Next.js Server (3 minute read)
item.description: A React Server Components flaw let an attacker force quadratic work while React rebuilt FormData for a server action, allowing a roughly 900 KB request to trigger 100 million string checks and block a Node.js event loop. The issue affects vulnerable React 19.0 to 19.2 releases and is fixed in 19.0.6, 19.1.7, and 19.2.6.

item.title: Your skills need an evaluation mechanism (11 minute read)
item.description: Expo built a CI evaluation harness that measures whether coding agents discover relevant skills, follow their guidance, and produce working apps. Adding an overview skill raised sessions loading at least one downstream Expo skill from 9% to 55%, while catalog crowding tests showed why names and opening descriptions must survive truncation.

item.title: The Slow Formation of Durable Software (16 minute read)
item.description: The origin story of Zotero shows how years of conversation, prototypes, and collaboration helped a team of historians discover what durable research software should become. Its path from Web Scrapbook and Scribe to a browser-aware tool used by millions argues that clear product vision can require slow communal formation, even when implementation itself becomes cheap.

item.title: Sentry + OTel: You can add connected context to your OTel signals. Here's how (Sponsor)
item.description: You can send your OTLP-compatible logs and traces directly to Sentry, with no extra dependencies. This workshop shows you how to use them for performance monitoring and debugging. Save your spot

item.title: calc-input, a custom input element that accepts mathematical formulas (4 minute read)
item.description: calc-input lets forms accept arithmetic expressions, shows formulas on focus and results on blur, and uses a safe parser plus native form validation instead of eval().

item.title: How much does it cost to use open source software? (3 minute read)
item.description: A Google study found most internal open source package updates take four hours or less, while local patches, dependencies, and upstream contributor counts better predicted difficult updates than package age or internal adoption.

item.title: The Bug Only My Screen Could See (10 minute read)
item.description: A display-only flicker that browser captures could not reproduce was traced to full-width tile repaints, then reduced from 267 page-tile repaints to 9 by promoting only the changing timeline elements to their own composited layers.

item.title: video-shotcraft (GitHub Repo)
item.description: video-shotcraft turns coding agents into a Remotion-based motion studio with 157 shot recipes, 214 motion previews, editable templates, sound design guidance, and a browser workbench.

item.title: AI agents are the primary readers of Mintlify-powered sites. (Sponsor)
item.description: In August, agents made 257 million web requests versus 131 million human page loads. Docs are only one surface. Agents also answer from help centers, changelogs, community forums, and support archives. In our survey of 329 professionals, 94% said their company has knowledge beyond docs, and just 7% have made all of it readable by agents. The 2026 State of Knowledge Report covers our 2,400-test navigation benchmark, how Anthropic runs Claude Code's docs, and what this means for how you maintain knowledge.Read the report

item.title: A Token Is Not a Message: Stop Storing AI Responses Like Event Logs (21 minute read)
item.description: Streaming tokens as event logs makes refreshed or late-joining clients rebuild partial responses, while rewriting one record for every token overloads the database. The article compares four storage patterns and argues that message appends can return the full response so far, continue live delivery, and save only the completed message to application storage.

item.title: A Hitchhiker's Guide to Postgres Text Search (14 minute read)
item.description: Cortex replaced a Lucene-based search architecture with PostgreSQL full-text search, a custom query parser, weighted ranking, and CDC-fed indexes. The change cut public API p95 latency from 13.3 seconds to 1.54 seconds, reduced total memory use by about 40%, and made most edits searchable within seconds.

item.title: Anti-Patterns in Software Blogging (10 minute read)
item.description: Software blogs lose readers when they meander, assume too much background knowledge, or outsource key explanations to links. The guide recommends stating the payoff in the title and opening sentences, writing for a specific reader, and keeping external references optional.

item.title: JPEG XL Finally Lands in Chrome! (3 minute read)
item.description: Chrome 155 will ship a memory-safe JPEG XL decoder built in Rust, reversing the browser's earlier decision to remove support. Chrome's reach could make the format mainstream, especially for high-fidelity photography, lossless compression, progressive decoding, and lossless JPEG transcoding.

item.title: Reasons to Dislike AI Coding (3 minute read)
item.description: The essay examines five objections to AI coding: code as art, job displacement, dehumanizing work, rule-based views of software engineering, and support for powerful AI companies. It argues that several critiques depend on debatable assumptions about what software work is for, while locating the strongest human concern in labor relations and control of production.

item.title: Got 2 minutes? (Sponsor)
item.description: Is your existing CMS holding you back? Drupal delivers an enterprise-grade, open-source foundation designed to power high-traffic, secure and future-proof digital experiences. Test the AI integrations, the decoupled flexibility, and see why 400k+ global sites trust it - 100% risk-free. Explore the free trial.

item.title: GPT-6 and Intelligent UI for Everyone (12 minute read)
item.description: GPT-6 is rolling out in ChatGPT with Intelligent UI, which can combine text, graphics, forms, charts, and interactive tools in a response. Paid tiers use GPT-6 Sol, Free and Go use GPT-6 Luna, and the release can begin responding while it continues reasoning or searching.

item.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 (Website)
item.description: Claude Haiku 5.5 targets high-volume, latency-sensitive work such as summarization, classification, browser use, and subagent tasks. Anthropic says average running costs are about 75% lower than Haiku 4.5, with adjustable effort and availability across its platform, AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure.

item.title: Docker Agent (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Docker Agent is a CLI plugin for defining and running AI agents from declarative YAML. It supports multi-agent orchestration, MCP and built-in tools, multiple model providers, retrieval, and packaging agents to OCI registries.

item.title: The Agentic Development Loop (5 minute read)
item.description: Agentic development changes the ideal linter because automated checks run on nearly every coding turn and agents can act on rules that humans might find too noisy. Ultracite pairs fast tools such as Oxlint and Oxfmt with strict rules and agent instructions, while keeping judgment-heavy questions for review.

item.title: I Gave Grok Bot a Remote Computer (8 minute read)
item.description: A remote Upstash Box gives Grok Bot a shell, persistent filesystem, GitHub integration, public previews, schedules, snapshots, and optional browser automation through MCP. The examples show it building a live app, cloning and fixing repositories, and turning a Slack report into a Linear ticket and pull request from a phone.

item.title: input type="password" maxlength="20" Prevents Me from Logging into Vanguard (2 minute read)
item.description: Vanguard's password reset form silently truncated pasted passwords at 20 characters, while its login form accepted the full value and then rejected it as incorrect. The incident shows why password length limits should be validated visibly in JavaScript or on the server instead of using an HTML maxlength attribute that changes the submitted credential.

item.title: Give your agent the web, free (Sponsor)
item.description: TinyFish is the all in one Webstack for agents. Give them the tools to search, extract, browse, and act on the web on one platform. Now claim your 30% bonus

item.title: We Moved Off Firestore. The Slow Page Stayed Slow (12 minute read)
item.description: A Firestore-to-SQL migration only became faster after the read model moved aggregation to the server, cutting a ten-year view from 56 seconds to 3.7 seconds and shrinking the shared search payload from 18.27 MB to 1.63 MB.

item.title: A Visual Notation for React's Parent and Owner Trees (22 minute read)
item.description: This visual notation distinguishes React's parent and owner trees so component structure and creation relationships can be read as diagrams instead of inferred from scattered code.

item.title: Size Limit (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Size Limit enforces JavaScript performance budgets in CI, including bundle size, dependency cost, and estimated download and execution time.

item.title: REA (GitHub Repo)
item.description: REA connects coding agents to local tools for reverse engineering websites, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and native binaries.
